issues.description: Document the HAS_TIME regex as a deliberate cheap pre-filter for valueParser.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged that /\dm?s/i is an over-approximating fast-path gating the authoritative valueParser walk. It will fire on substrings inside urls/strings (harmless — slow path validates) and is an implicit second specification of 'contains a time token'. A one-line comment naming it as a pre-filter and noting any new time units must update both sites prevents future drift.

issues.description: Add a regression test pinning the early-return behavior.
issues.detail: The patch is a behavior-preserving optimization, but no test guards against the fast-path skipping a real violation (odd whitespace, casing, vendor prefixes on the value side). One targeted test locking in that the regex gate never drops a value the parser would flag would harden the change. Not blocking.

synthesis.summary: The panel unanimously accepts this patch as a small, well-shaped performance fix: a cheap regex short-circuits the expensive valueParser walk when no time token is present, and reordering `vendor.unprefixed`/`toLowerCase` after the guard avoids needless work on skipped decls. Correctness is preserved because the slow path still validates any value that passes the gate. The only consensus concern is documentation: the regex is an implicit, over-approximating second spec of 'contains a time token' and deserves a one-line comment. A regression test pinning the early-return is a nice-to-have. Land it.
